color.why: Both restore the warm palette and excellent measured text contrast; Y has a small non-state brass step numeral (Y:285), but neither dilutes the accent materially.

typography.why: Both use Geist language/mono data, balanced display wrapping and bounded readable copy. Y has a crisper shorter hero; X has a more restrained display scale (X:271–287; Y:140–147).

layout.why: Y shows captioned work in the opening viewport and exposes all mobile navigation labels; X spends the entire opening viewport before any sample and clips the mobile final nav label (page-1440.png and page-390.png in each shots directory).

accessibility.why: Both have zero supplied axe violations, landmarks, alt, real controls and live copy status. X focus outline is visibly clipped by nav overflow; Y focus is intact, but its comparison ledger hides the column meaning from assistive technology (X:178–184; Y:443–456).

states.why: Both provide actionable copy fallback and copied feedback. Y adds visible inline failure/status feedback and a complete focus outline; X announces failure only in hidden status and clips nav focus (X:753,790–793; Y:529–548; focus screenshots).

copy.why: Both replace false AI-platform claims with accurate code-rendering facts and the source voice. Y supplies sample captions and more complete Desk/QA/final facts; its hero copy command still lacks immediate setup context (X:601–752; Y:390–503).

motion.why: Neither has infinite motion or layout-property animation. X retains an unsolicited staggered 500ms entrance and button scale under reduced motion; Y uses restrained hover light/fade and reduces the long transitions and smooth scroll (X:238,561–577; Y:362–366; both metrics).

ux.why: Both make the studio credible and preserve identity. Y better demonstrates the work and offers a literal command action; X still hides all work below the first screen and retains a generic three-card structure, while its Start the Desk link merely scrolls (X:603–607,634–650).

X: Navigation overflow clips the brass keyboard outline at its top/bottom, visible in X/shots/focus-tab3-1440.png; X/index.html:178–184,188–193. At 390px the last navigation label is also concealed behind the fade (X/shots/page-390.png).
The primary label Start the Desk implies execution but only navigates to instructions, X/index.html:603–604. Prefer a label describing setup or a literal copy action.

Mobile command wells horizontally scroll their code at the narrow width rather than making the complete command immediately readable, X/index.html:499–515 and X/shots/page-390-full.png; pnpm studio:doctor is visibly clipped.
Y: Hero offers pnpm desk:start before installation/prerequisites, with no direct setup CTA beside it; Y/index.html:393–397 versus prerequisites at 491–500. A fresh checkout user can copy the wrong first command.

The This is / This is not comparison header is aria-hidden and the desktop descriptions contain no explicit negation; definition-list semantics present an opposite as the definition. Y/index.html:443–456; the Not prefix is mobile-only CSS at 262–265.
The final process step numeral is permanently brass without being current, selected or waiting for a real approval, Y/index.html:285; minor One Brass Rule deviation (DESIGN.md:163).

overall.why: I would ship Y because its captioned samples enter the first viewport, its mobile navigation stays legible, and the page explains the code-rendered studio with a concrete action. It preserves the dark screening-room identity while offering more complete visible feedback and quieter reduced-motion behavior. Before release, connect the hero command to setup prerequisites and make the comparison ledger’s negative meaning explicit to assistive technology.
